correctness.rationale: The decomposition into one k[t]/t² factor and finite matrix factors is justified by the odd-order Fourier-character structure and finite-field splitting. The 2×2 centralizer calculation forces any commuting square-zero matrices into a common nilpotent line, hence zero product. Each line contributes exactly Q^r-1 nonzero coefficient tuples, with Q+1 possible lines; direct multiplication and regular-left rank give every polynomial factor. Maximal subspaces follow by coordinate projections and geometric irreducibility by Segre–Veronese cones. Six original group-multiplication pair enumerations and two triple enumerations agree; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The full 2014 Makhijani–Sharma–Srivastava theorem already supplies the algebra factorization; univariate counts and unit-group structure are explicitly excluded from the novel scope. The assessed finding is the all-arity multivariate left-rank compatibility census and exact maximal compatible-subspace count. The inspected Ngo–Šivic source addresses unrestricted matrix tuple geometry. Accessible published-finding corpus findings and prior claims did not show an equivalent or dominating joint-rank formula. Historical uniqueness remains provisional: a more general unlocated finite-field matrix-cone point-count theorem could subsume this arithmetic application.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete, all-arity and all-ranks joint distribution of compatible square-zero multiplication maps and the maximal compatible subgroup geometry. For example, the C9 and C3×C3 odd kernels have equal order nine and equal individual square-zero counts 512 but different compatible ordered-pair counts 22,720 and 40,000, demonstrating an intrinsic invariant missed by univariate counts. This is a motivated exact arithmetic classification, not an arbitrary computation.
